options.name: api_key
options.description: API key of your NetOrca team. The NetOrca API supports API-key authentication only - there is no username/password mode. Treat the key like a password - supply it via the E(NETORCA_API_KEY) environment variable (for example from a CI/CD secret) or from Ansible Vault, never as a literal in a playbook. If not set, the value of the E(NETORCA_API_KEY) environment variable is used.

options.name: api_url
options.description: Base URL of the NetOrca API, for example C(https://api.example.netorca.io). The URL is normalised to end in a single C(/v1), so passing it with or without the suffix both work. If not set, the value of the E(NETORCA_API_URL) environment variable is used.

options.name: application_id
options.description: Filter by ID of the consumer application the change belongs to.

options.name: change_type
options.description: Filter by type of change. A V(DELETE) change that completes moves its service item to the C(DECOMMISSIONED) runtime state - poll for these to decommission infrastructure.

options.name: commit_id
options.description: Filter by the Git commit ID recorded on the submission (substring match) - traces a merge in the consumer's repository to the changes it produced.

options.name: consumer_team_id
options.description: Filter by ID of the consuming team that requested the change.

options.name: context
options.description: Point of view for the request. The same query returns different data depending on which side of the service relationship your team is on. V(serviceowner) operates on the services your team I(offers) - the requests made against them, their service items and deployed items. This is the side that validates, approves, deploys and completes changes. V(consumer) operates on what your team I(consumes) - the service items your applications declared and the change instances tracking your own requests. If

options.name: declaration
options.description: Filter by exact match on fields of the change's new declaration, for example C({"partition": "prod"}).

options.name: declaration_contains
options.description: Filter by containment match on fields of the change's new declaration.

options.name: declaration_regex
options.description: Filter by regular expression match on fields of the change's new declaration, for example C({"name": "^prod-.*"}).

options.name: dependant
options.description: Query the dependant view (C(change_instances/dependant)) instead of the plain listing. Lists the dependant copies of change instances assigned to your team because the service declares your team in its C(dependant_teams) (see the NetOrca documentation on dependant teams).

options.name: exclude_referenced
options.description: Exclude referenced change instances - V(MODIFY) changes raised on a service item only because another service item its declaration references was changed. Enable this to list just the changes consumers made directly.

options.name: id
options.description: Return only the change instance with this ID. When set, all other filters are ignored. If the ID does not exist, an empty list is returned.

options.name: include_history
options.description: Also return the state history of the change instance selected by O(id) - the audit trail of every transition the change went through, with actor and timestamp.

options.name: limit
options.description: Maximum number of results to return. Results are auto-paginated, so by default all matching records are returned regardless of the API's page size.

options.name: modified_after
options.description: Only return change instances modified at or after this ISO 8601 timestamp, for example C(2026-07-01T00:00:00Z). Useful for incremental polling - fetch only what moved since the previous run.

options.name: ordering
options.description: Server-side field to order results by, for example V(created) or V(modified). Prefix with C(-) for descending order - V(-modified) returns the most recently changed records first.

options.name: referenced
options.description: Query the referenced view (C(change_instances/referenced)) instead of the plain listing, returning only the referenced change instances described under O(exclude_referenced).

options.name: service_id
options.description: Filter by service ID.

options.name: service_item_id
options.description: Filter by ID of the service item the change applies to.

options.name: service_name
options.description: Filter by exact service name, for example V(LOAD_BALANCER). Usually the first filter a service owner sets when polling their work queue.

options.name: service_owner_team_id
options.description: Filter by ID of the team that owns the service.

options.name: state
options.description: Filter by change instance state. Any combination can be requested - for example V(PENDING) plus V(APPROVED) is everything still open.

options.name: submission_id
options.description: Filter by ID of the consumer submission that created the change.

options.name: validate_certs
options.description: Whether to validate TLS certificates when talking to the API. Only disable this for lab instances with self-signed certificates. If not set, the value of the E(NETORCA_VALIDATE_CERTS) environment variable is used.
